sections.title: Sound of letter dáblio
paragraphs: The letter is called (dáblio) /ˈdabliu/. Its main sound is heard in the borrowed word (web) /ˈwɛb/. This letter has two different sounds in Portuguese words. Both sounds appear in words taken from other languages.

sections.title: Pronouncing letter dáblio
paragraphs: For the first sound, make a small circle with your lips. Pull the back of your tongue up near the roof of your mouth. Turn your voice on and let the air flow smoothly. For the second sound, touch your lower lip to your upper teeth. Push the air through the narrow gap with your voice turned on. Touch your throat to feel it shake.

sections.title: Spelling of letter dáblio
paragraphs: You use the first sound in words from English, as in (whisky) /ˈwiʃki/. You use the second sound in words from German, as in (watt) /ˈvat/. Names from German origin also take this sound, as in (Wagner) /ˈvaɡnɛɾ/.

sections.title: Avoiding mistakes with dáblio
paragraphs: Do not confuse the two sounds. Do not use the sound of vine when you say a word from English like water. Do not use the sound of water when you say a word from German like vine. Match the sound to where the word comes from.
